title: Counits, transposes and composition under adjoint-equivalence conjugation
statement:
Let $\mathscr C_i,\mathscr N_i$ ($i=1,2,3$) be categories in fixed universes [def-nagata-category]. For each $i$, specify functors $R_i:\mathscr C_i\to\mathscr N_i$, $L_i:\mathscr N_i\to\mathscr C_i$ and an adjunction $R_i\dashv L_i$ whose unit $u_i:1\to L_iR_i$ and counit $e_i:R_iL_i\to1$ are natural isomorphisms satisfying the triangle identities. Use the reverse adjunction $L_i\dashv R_i$ with unit $e_i^{-1}$ and counit $u_i^{-1}$. Composition is written right to left. For any functor $F:\mathscr N_i\to\mathscr N_j$, define $\bar F=L_jFR_i$, and for a natural transformation $\alpha:F\to F'$ define $\bar\alpha=L_j\alpha R_i$. Define the natural isomorphism
$$c_{F,P}=L_jF(e_{i,P}):\bar F L_iP\longrightarrow L_jFP.$$
For every adjunction $F:\mathscr N_1\rightleftarrows\mathscr N_2:G$ with counit $\epsilon$, form the composite adjunction $\bar F\dashv\bar G$ from $R_1\dashv L_1$, $F\dashv G$, and $L_2\dashv R_2$ [def-weil-pbc-composite-adjunction]. Its counit is
$$\bar\epsilon_K=u_{2,K}^{-1}\circ L_2(\epsilon_{R_2K})\circ L_2F(e_{1,GR_2K})\qquad(K\in\mathscr C_2).$$
For $P\in\mathscr N_1$, $N\in\mathscr N_2$ and $a:P\to GN$, the adjoint transpose of $c_{G,N}^{-1}\circ L_1(a):L_1P\to\bar G L_2N$ is
$$L_2(\epsilon_N\circ F(a))\circ c_{F,P}:\bar F L_1P\longrightarrow L_2N.$$
The identifications $c_F,c_G$ are natural in all object maps and in transformations of the functors. For arbitrary $F:\mathscr N_1\to\mathscr N_2$ and $H:\mathscr N_2\to\mathscr N_3$, the maps
$$\kappa_{H,F,K}=L_3H(e_{2,FR_1K}):\bar H\bar F K\longrightarrow\overline{HF}K$$
form a natural isomorphism. For $\alpha:F\to F'$ and $\beta:H\to H'$, writing $*$ for horizontal composition of natural transformations, one has
$$\overline{\beta*\alpha}\circ\kappa_{H,F}=\kappa_{H',F'}\circ(\bar\beta*\bar\alpha).$$
No additive, derived, sheaf-theoretic or nonemptiness hypothesis on these categories is needed.
